9.question: A daycare posts that its “Mozart-and-flashcards package *causes* earlier formal operations,” citing toddlers who sat through the package and later named more shapes than waitlisted peers whose parents opted out. Staff also praise kids using adult-like conservation talk after heavy prompting. A methods consultant and a Piagetian disagree. Best evaluation?
options: Opt-in versus opt-out groups are non-equivalent, and prompted jargon is not spontaneous formal operations; causal claims about Mozart packages
Any shape-naming gain after enrichment proves formal operations arrived, because vocabulary count is identical to abstract hypothetical-deductive
Waitlists are automatic random assignment when parents self-select, so internal validity threats cannot apply to infant enrichment product claims
Conservation prompted by adults is assimilation of schemas into object permanence alone, which validates acceleration into formal operations
9.correctFeedback: Selection confounds plus mistaking prompted talk for stage attainment undermine the ad (§9.2–9.3; methods; thinking).

wrongFeedback.1: People who pick this equate word counts with formal-operational reasoning.
wrongFeedback.2: People who pick this treat parental opt-out as randomization.
wrongFeedback.3: People who pick this scramble Piagetian concepts to rubber-stamp acceleration claims.

Any daycare crying proves disorganized attachment, so extinction of proximity-seeking is required before exploratory behavior can emerge in the
Continuous candy for silence classically conditions the internal working model into secure attachment within one week of drop-offs without
Secure base behavior is a flashbulb memory for faces, therefore reinforcement schedules alone determine attachment classification better than
9.correctFeedback: Attachment assessment emphasizes reunion/secure base, not crying alone; harsh extinction/candy hacks miss the construct (§9.3; learning; memory).

wrongFeedback.1: People who pick this over-diagnose from protest alone and misuse extinction.
wrongFeedback.2: People who pick this invent classical candy conditioning of working models.
wrongFeedback.3: People who pick this replace attachment observation with flashbulb/reinforcement myths.

9.question: A prenatal clinic sees a client drinking heavily early in pregnancy who asks whether “genes alone decide IQ, so alcohol advice is moralizing.” Staff review teratogen timing, synaptogenesis vulnerability, and that heritability ≠ immutability. Which reply is most accurate?

If IQ is heritable at all, teratogens cannot affect cognitive outcomes, because heritability coefficients convert directly into destiny ratios

Sensitive periods are identical to critical periods for language phonemes only, so ethanol exposure after week four is developmentally irrelevant
9.correctFeedback: Teratogens can alter developmental trajectories; heritability does not license prenatal alcohol exposure (§9.1–9.2; biopsych).

wrongFeedback.2: People who pick this trivialize alcohol as a maternal taste issue only.
wrongFeedback.3: People who pick this wrongly narrow sensitive periods to phonemes alone.

10.question: In a dating-lab demo, participants pedal bikes to raise arousal, then rate a neutral confederate as more attractive (excitation-transfer style). One student says James–Lange means arousal *is* attraction; another says Cannon–Bard proves cortex labels first; a third cites misattribution. Best statement?
options: Residual arousal can be misattributed to a salient social target; that supports two-factor/misattribution ideas more than equating raw arousal
James–Lange requires bike arousal to be attraction even without any cognitive appraisal or situational cue about the confederate in the vignette
Cannon–Bard claims the cortex must finish labeling before any autonomic arousal begins, so bike-then-rating designs cannot produce misattribution
Excitation transfer stores attraction as a procedural engram in the NMJ, making appraisal theories irrelevant to the ratings collected now
10.correctFeedback: Misattribution/excitation transfer: arousal + appraisal cues shape felt attraction (§10.4; biopsych; memory systems literacy).

wrongFeedback.1: People who pick this collapse James–Lange into “arousal equals attraction” without appraisal.
wrongFeedback.2: People who pick this caricature Cannon–Bard timing to rule out misattribution.
wrongFeedback.3: People who pick this invent NMJ procedural storage for romantic ratings.
